newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares fall in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares fall in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares fell on Tuesday on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE), continuing a downward trend since the company made a $77-million issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) last week.
A shares fell 2.26 percent to $110.5 from Monday's $113 and B shares fell 1.6 percent to $114.25 from $116.125.
It was biggest dip in the shares' prices in four consecutive days that A shares have fallen -- the third day for B shares -- since Thursday, a day after the GDR issue.

The GDRs, each of which nominally represents one-tenth of an A share, were last quoted at $11.6 on the London Stock Exchange Automated Quotation system (SEAQ). They allow non-Arab investors access to the market in Solidere for the first time.
Turnover in Solidere shares was 11,739 shares from 9,000 on Monday and value was $1,316,855 from $1,024,798.375.
There was no trade in the shares of the four other companies listed on BSE: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.55 percent to 82.45 and the BLOM stock index fell 1.53 percent to 952.33.
